subject: Single season model and goodness-of-fit issues

messages.author: f83823b583ab85c7
messages.subject: Single season model and goodness-of-fit issues
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to fit some single season occupancy models on capture data of Emys orbicularis (European pond turtle) but I have issues concerning the goodness of fit (gof) of my best model (in terms of AICc).
I've seen articles saying that I only have to test the gof of my most complexe model but I have very few individuals (12 sites) so I'm juste testing models with 1-2 variables. So instead I tested the gof of my best model.
I'm unsig mb.gof.test() from AICcmodavg package which gives me p-value = 0.002 and c-hat = 7.7.
I tried using AICc for my model selection but it's not really a solution to my problem.

Is there anything I can try to "save" this analysis or is my model just fitting to baddly to the data ?

Thanks for reading, I'm open to any suggestions or thoughts on this issue,

Best regards,
Julie

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Single season model and goodness-of-fit issues
parts:
Dear Julie,

 

Unfortunately, that looks like a gigantic value for c-hat. Could you share the data with the list ? Or off-list ? Or show what summary(name_of_your_unmarkedframe) yields ? One might hope to get some ideas about how the model could be improved by looking at the data.

 

On the other hand, with just 12 sites, it may well be that there is not so much that can be saved.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

As I have not only presence-absence data but also count data (number of captures), I tried to fit some N-mixture models with a negative-binomial mixture which seems to provide a better fit. I still have to study this subject to make sure I haven't made any mistakes.

Julie
